The solution has the right overall idea: the roots of \(P\) are \(r_i^2\), and evaluating the resulting products via \(Q(1),Q(-1),Q(i),Q(-i)\) gives the correct value
\[
-\frac{2004\cdot2006}{1+2005^2}
=-\frac{2010012}{2010013}.
\]

However, there are algebraic/typographical errors in the intermediate product manipulation, especially the fourth displayed line: the factors involving \(i\) are not written consistently, and the transition to \(Q(1)Q(-1)/(Q(i)Q(-i))\) is not properly justified as written. A cleaner derivation is
\[
\frac{P(1)}{P(-1)}
=-\prod_i\frac{(1-r_i)(1+r_i)}{(i-r_i)(-i-r_i)}
=-\frac{Q(1)Q(-1)}{Q(i)Q(-i)},
\]
with the signs then checked carefully. Thus the conclusion is correct, but the exposition should be corrected and the sign manipulations made more rigorous.
